subject.title: [Bug]: TLS certificate pin mismatch loop when connecting through Cloudflare Tunnel/Access (anycast edge certs)

question: What TLS identity policy should iOS Remote Domain mode use for a manually entered, CA-valid public hostname that may serve multiple rotating or anycast leaf certificates?
rationale: The existing single-leaf TOFU model cannot reliably support Cloudflare anycast, but relaxing it globally could weaken protections intended for local, discovered, self-signed, or explicitly pinned gateways.

options.title: Split trust by route provenance
options.body: Use platform CA and hostname validation for CA-valid Remote Domain endpoints while preserving explicit pins for discovered, local, setup-code, and self-signed routes.

options.title: Support a bounded pin set
options.body: Keep TOFU semantics but persist multiple user-approved fingerprints with explicit replacement, expiry, and pruning behavior.

options.title: Keep strict leaf pinning
options.body: Retain the current security model and explicitly document rotating or anycast reverse-proxy TLS as unsupported for iOS Remote Domain mode.

recommendation.title: Split trust by route provenance
recommendation.body: Use platform CA and hostname validation for CA-valid Remote Domain endpoints while preserving explicit pins for discovered, local, setup-code, and self-signed routes.

likelyOwner.reason: The current certificate-rotation prompt and replacement behavior appears to originate in their merged iOS gateway work.
